card.statement:
A poset $\cal P$ is unitarily representation-finite if it has only a finite number of nonisometric $\cal P$-systems that are unitarily indecomposable.

-
A poset $\cal P$ is unitarily wild if the problem of classifying $\cal P$-systems up to isometry contains the problem of classifying operators on unitary spaces. The posets that are not unitarily wild are called unitarily tame (in analogy with
the partition of animals into
wild and tame ones).
card.label: Definition 3

paper.title: Systems of subspaces of a unitary space
paper.abstract: For a given poset, we consider its representations by systems of subspaces of a unitary space ordered by inclusion. We classify such systems for all posets for which an explicit classification is possible.
